claim_en: THE PLAINS OF MOAB — THE BOOK'S LAST CAMP; BALAK SAW THE CONQUEST. 'And the children of Israel journeyed and camped in the plains of Moab across the Jordan of Jericho' (22:1 — Chukat's last verse, read with this draft): from here the book never moves — nine datelines 'in the plains of Moab' to 36:13, 'the Jordan of Jericho' seven, and Moses climbs FROM the plains of Moab to die (Deut 34:1) (computed); 'Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorite' (22:2) — chapter 21's Sihon war the antecedent; the full name at 22:2, 10, 16 and Joshua 24:9; Balak thirty-nine seats, only Joshua 24:9 and Micah 6:5 outside Numbers (computed).
middah: ink (the datelines and the name's seats computed)

'And Moab FEARED before the people' (22:3) — the token is Abraham's 'and he SOJOURNED in Gerar' (Gen 20:1), one skin for dwelling and dread; 'and Moab LOATHED the children of Israel' — the verb of 21:5 'our soul LOATHES the light bread', Rebekah's 'I loathe my life' (Gen 27:46), the land's 'I loathed them' (Lev 20:23): Israel loathed the manna, Moab loathes Israel (computed on the points); 'the assembly will LICK UP all our surroundings as the ox licks the green of the field' (22:4) — the lick-verb's one Torah seat (Elijah's fire 'licked up the water', 1 Kgs 18:38); 'Moab said to THE ELDERS OF MIDIAN' (one seat) — Midian enters at 22:4 and 22:7, vanishes through the oracles, returns with Cozbi (25:6-18): the ink's thread to chapter 31 (computed). Onkelos: 'loathed' → DISTRESS; 'lick up' → DESTROY (cut).
middah: ink (the two verbs' kin by the points, the lick-verb's one seat and Midian's seats computed)

'He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, to Pethor which is by the river' (22:5) — Balaam's full name five seats (his death 31:8 among them); Pethor's two seats, Deut 23:5 'from Pethor of ARAM-NAHARAIM'; ONKELOS writes 'Pethor ARAM which is on the EUPHRATES' — the retelling's Aram and the river's name inserted into the verse (cut from the shelf's bytes); 'behold, it has covered THE EYE OF THE LAND' — THE LOCUSTS' CLAUSE (Exod 10:5 'and it shall cover the eye of the land'), the phrase's three seats: the plague, Balak's message (22:5) and Balaam's report (22:11); Onkelos adds 'the sun' at both (computed, cut); 'come, CURSE this people for me' (22:6) — the first of THREE CURSE-ROOTS: arar seven tokens, qabab ten, za'am three — twenty curse-words in a portion where no curse is spoken; 'whom you bless is blessed and whom you curse is cursed' — 'whom you bless is blessed' one seat, the patriarchs' formula returned at 24:9 in Isaac's form reversed (computed). Onkelos: 'strike' → WAGE WAR (cut).
middah: E10 (the repeated expression — the locusts' clause at Balak's message; the curse-roots counted; the translation's names cut)

claim_en: DIVINATIONS IN THEIR HAND; GOD CAME TO BALAAM — THE THREE GENTILES' VERSE; THE LORD REFUSES — PHARAOH'S VERB. 'The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with DIVINATIONS in their hand' (22:7) — the noun's Torah four: here, 23:23 'no divination in Israel', Deut 18:10 and 18:14's ban; Joshua names him 'Balaam THE DIVINER' (13:22) (computed); 'lodge here the night... as THE LORD speaks to me' (22:8) — Balaam's mouth says the LORD (sixteen tokens in the chapter) while the narrator says GOD came (22:9, 20); 'AND GOD CAME TO Balaam' (22:9) — the clause's four seats in the Bible: Abimelech 'in a dream of the night' (Gen 20:3), Laban the Aramean 'in a dream of the night' (Gen 31:24), Balaam here and 'at night' at 22:20 — three gentiles visited by night, never an Israelite in that clause (computed); Onkelos makes each coming 'a WORD from before the LORD' and 22:10's 'to God' 'BEFORE THE LORD' (cut); 'you shall not go... you shall not curse the people, for it is blessed' (22:12); 'THE LORD REFUSES to let me go with you' (22:13, one seat) — the refusal-verb is PHARAOH's five times ('you refuse to let My people go', Exod 7:14, 7:27, 9:2, 10:3-4), then Jacob's, Joseph's, Edom's (20:21): the refuser refused (computed); Onkelos: 'there is NO WILL before the LORD' (cut).
middah: ink (the divination-noun's four, the coming-clause's four and the refusal-verb's seats computed; the translation's Word cut)

'Balak sent yet again princes, more and weightier' (22:15); 'thus says Balak... do not be HELD BACK from coming to me' (22:16) — the hold-back verb returns at 24:11, 'the LORD has held you back from honor'; 'I will surely HONOR you greatly' (22:17) — the doubled verb at two seats, 22:17 and 24:11's revocation (computed); 'if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold' (22:18) — the clause at 22:18 and 24:13, the deltas computed: here 'small or great' and 'the LORD MY GOD', there 'good or bad', 'from my own heart', no 'my God'; Onkelos: 'the mouth of the LORD' → the DECREE of the WORD of the LORD (cut); 'stay here, you too, the night' (22:19) — the second night; 'and God came to Balaam AT NIGHT: if the men have come to call you, rise, go with them; but ONLY the word that I speak to you, that you shall DO' (22:20) — THE WORD-FORMULA's first of six, the verb 'do', the restrictor 'only' (akh); 22:35 repeats it with 'nothing but' (efes) and the verb 'speak' (computed on the six).

'And Balaam rose in the morning and SADDLED his she-ass' (22:21) — Abraham's verse: 'and Abraham rose early in the morning and SADDLED his ass' (Gen 22:3), the saddling-verb's two Torah seats (Lev 8:13 'he bound caps' the homograph), and 'his TWO YOUNG MEN with him' (22:22) is Gen 22:3's 'his two young men with him' — the chapter of the binding and the chapter of the ass share their morning; the she-ass fourteen times in the chapter, the Torah's others Abraham's, Jacob's, Joseph's (computed); 'and God's anger burned because he was going' (22:22) — the portion's first of THREE angers (God's at Balaam's going, Balak's at Balaam 24:10, the LORD's at Israel 25:3); 'the angel of the LORD stationed himself in the way AS AN ADVERSARY to him' — the satan-word's two seats in the Torah, 22:22 and 22:32, both here (Job's and Zechariah's the Writings'); 'THE ANGEL OF THE LORD' ten times in this chapter, and in the Torah only at Hagar's well, the Akedah and the bush besides (computed). Onkelos: 'saddled' → READIED (cut).
middah: E10 (the repeated expression — the Akedah's morning and its two young men at Balaam's; the satan-word's and the angel's seats computed)
